content.content:
A ref-path entry underlines its characters while the pointer is over it.

In the detail panel's Content section a path entry is presented as a link (squvoxyr); this decision gives that link one further appearance state. While the pointer rests over the entry, the path's characters carry an underline. The underline follows the pointer's presence and nothing else: arriving over the entry puts it there, leaving takes it away, and the entry is drawn as it was before the pointer came. The entry is the same link before the pointer arrives and after it leaves — hovering does not create the link, does not make an entry activatable that was not one, and changes nothing about what activation is or what it leads to; it adds a mark to an entry that already carries the link look.

The underline is the whole of what changes. The entry's text stays the path the block already shows, as squvoxyr fixed it: the underline marks the characters the entry already shows, and while hovered the path is neither shortened, relabelled nor replaced, and no file name, directory summary, label, quoted title, icon or "open" control appears beside it, over it or in its place. Nor does the mark reach beyond the entry's own characters: it does not run across the block, the section's label or the value's frame, and it marks no other path in the block. What distinguishes the hovered entry from the other characters of the block is that mark on the path and nothing else this decision adds.

Underlined is exactly the population squvoxyr made a link: the entries the Content section shows for a value whose content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths, each path being an entry rptlovpt makes activatable (rptlovpt, squvoxyr). The content type shown beside the paths names the type and is neither a path nor an entry, so it gains nothing here; a path mentioned anywhere else — inside the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, or elsewhere in the panel — gains nothing here either. The state belongs to the entry under the pointer: hovering one path entry underlines that entry, while the other entries of the same block and the rest of the panel keep their resting appearance.

This is the hover state and no more than it. The entry's colour at rest and while hovered, the pointer's own appearance over it, the marker it carries while it has keyboard focus — a different state at a different time — and the vocabulary that names the entry are settled where they are owned; nothing here requires, forbids or implies any of them, and none of them may be read off the underline. Nothing here names or invents a class, a selector, a style property or a stylesheet rule, and nothing here adds an element to the block or settles the block's layout.

This decision neither extends nor narrows which entries squvoxyr presents as links, and it states nothing about a path that names no file: squvoxyr left such a path where rptlovpt left it, and nothing here requires or forbids that such a path be underlined. Nor does anything here restate, narrow or extend what a path entry is or what activating one does (rptlovpt).
content.rationale:
squvoxyr gave every ref-path entry the link look at rest and stopped there, so the entry makes its promise once and then the block goes quiet under the pointer: a reader moving across two or three paths in the same block has nothing but the pointer's position to say which entry it is on. This decision adds the one cheapest answer — while the pointer is over an entry, that entry's own characters are underlined — so the pointer's position comes back as a fact about the entry rather than something to be inferred, and it does so with no new element, no change to the path's text and no change to what the entry is or to what activating it does. The underline is the smallest hover state available: it borrows a convention readers already apply to text they can follow, and it appears and disappears with the pointer while everything else about the entry stays where squvoxyr and rptlovpt put it.

Stopping at "underlined while hovered" is what keeps the rest decidable and keeps this decision off its neighbours' subjects. The entry's colour, the pointer's own appearance over it, the marker that shows the entry holds keyboard focus and the vocabulary that names the entry are each a stylesheet fact a reviewer can point at, and each belongs to the decision that owns it; settled here they would be restated or contradicted there, and the distinction between a hover state and the link it decorates would be lost. Kept to one state, this node leaves each of those to be argued and checked on its own evidence, and leaves the block's structure, its layout and the activation rptlovpt fixed exactly as recorded.

The commitment is one state of the entry and not a re-decision of the entry, which is what the licence over squvoxyr requires: the link look is the entry's whenever the pointer is elsewhere, the underline is added while the pointer is on it, and nothing here makes the link conditional on the hover, shows it only while hovered, or presents the hover as the thing that tells a reader the path is an entry. A reviewer can refute the commitment with a single observation — the pointer is over a path entry and that entry's characters carry no underline, or the underline is drawn somewhere other than the entry's own text — without supplying a rule this node or its prerequisite does not state.
